title: A selection box on the timeline scrolls the timeline when it reaches an edge
goal: While dragging a selection box on the timeline, bringing the pointer near the left, right, top or bottom edge scrolls the timeline that way so the box can reach things off screen. It starts slowly just inside the edge and speeds up the closer the pointer gets, without ever becoming hard to control, and the box keeps growing with the scroll.
notes:
User's words: "marquee selection on the timeline doesn't seem to have progressive scroll built in - where as we get close to the scroll edge it starts to slowly scroll in that direction so that we can select more items offscreen. as you get closer to the edge, the velocity increases but not obnoxiously".

From code reading (not run): vertical edge autoscroll exists only for carrying a track, TrackRowDragSession.swift:238-263 (edgeBand, edgeSpeed, speed = edgeSpeed * into * |into|, driven per frame with dt, scrolls editor.timelineTracksScroll and moves the pointer by the scrolled amount), and LayerRowDragSession.swift:293-300 for the layers list. The box: EditorState+TrackRange.swift LanePress/LaneBox and beginLanePress/endLanePress, gesture TimelineLaneMarquee (TimelineTrackRows.swift ~1010+), drawn by TimelineLaneBoxView (TimelineDock.swift ~1291); its range is in ms, so a horizontal scroll must extend the box's ms range by the scrolled time. A drag gesture gets no events while the pointer is still, so autoscroll needs a display-link/timer driver like TrackRowDragSession's. Box selection itself: dragging-a-box-on-the-timeline-picks-everything (done).
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: zoom the timeline in so clips run off both sides and tracks overflow vertically, drag a box toward each edge and record that nothing scrolls

The edge scrolling the track drag already has (TrackRowDragSession autoscroll: an edge band, speed rising with the square of how far into the band the pointer is) moves into one shared, pure, unit tested helper in PhotonzCore (tests first) and both the track drag and the box use it
Horizontal: near the left or right edge of the tracks' visible area the timeline scrolls in time; vertical: near the top or bottom it scrolls the tracks; both at once in a corner

Feel, MEASURED and written in the audit: zero speed at the inner edge of the band, a gentle start (well under a fifth of top speed across the inner half of the band), top speed only at or past the edge, and a top speed chosen so a 10 minute timeline at a typical zoom can be crossed in a few seconds while a single clip is still easy to stop on; the curve and its numbers are in the audit

Holding the pointer still in the band keeps scrolling and the box keeps extending to the pointer's place in the scrolled content; moving back out of the band stops it at once; letting go picks everything the box covered, including what scrolled into view
Pointer past the edge of the window (outside the timeline) keeps scrolling at top speed in that direction until released
Dragging clips, zoom bars and title bars along the timeline gets the same edge scrolling if it does not have it already (the audit says which had it)
Scrolling is smooth at 60 fps (frame timing MEASURED over a 5 s scroll) and never fights the playhead or follow-playhead
A walk draws a box from a clip on screen to one off screen to the right, holding at the edge, and checks both are picked
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Reproduced at Next defaults (no flags): sample recording + Sample Music, timeline zoomed in twice (0:00 to 0:03 on screen). windowDrag from (400,963) to (1722,930), past the lanes' right edge, held: the box stops at the edge and the window still reads 0:00 to 0:03, nothing scrolls (/tmp/photonz-playtest/edge-autoscroll-repro/1-held-at-right-edge-sc.png). Vertical: the lane press has no autoscroll code at all (only TrackRowDragSession/LayerRowDragSession do).
owns these walks: box-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk, box-scrolls-at-the-edge-by-hand-walk, zoom-bar-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk

Adversarial review before building: (1) A press that starts inside an edge band would scroll instantly with no hand movement; fixed by arming each band only after the pointer has been outside it (past the edge always scrolls). (2) The box told a new press from an old one by the moment under the press, which changes once time scrolls, so a scroll would have restarted the box; it now compares the gesture's start point. (3) A drag gesture hears nothing while the pointer is still, so a display-link ticker drives the scroll from the last place the hand was. (4) Follow-playhead could fight the hand; it is held off during a run. Premiere and Final Cut both edge-scroll while marqueeing or dragging clips, so this meets the expectation.

Built: EdgeAutoscroll in PhotonzCore (cube curve, arming, time preset 1.5 lanes/s with band 40, rows preset 600 pt/s band 24; EdgeAutoscrollTests). TimelineEdgeScroll (Sources/Photonz) is one CADisplayLink ticker at 60 Hz shared by the box (EditorState+TrackRange laneBoxHand), clip bars, titles and caption cues through ClipPiecesBar (clipBarDragHand: body, piece carry, trims; vertical too for carries on the dock) and zoom bars (ZoomLane, zoomDragHand). TrackRowDragSession now uses EdgeAutoscroll.rows. Which had edge scrolling before: only the track carried by its header (vertical); clips, titles, zoom bars and the box had none.

Found while walking: after any clip drag the window jumped back to the playhead, because documentMomentChanged always ran followTimelineWindow. Now it follows only when the playhead has moved (timelineFollowedMS), so an edge scroll survives the let go. Every zoomed-timeline walk still passes (open-out-the-timeline, first-long-jump-when-zoomed-in, clip-pictures-when-zoomed-in, ruler-names-the-right-time-zoomed, a-click-on-a-clip-piece-picks-it, the-timeline-is-the-one-in-the-mock).

Walks: box-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk (scripted boxToEdge step, survives a lock, no flags: right, left, bottom, 5 s timing), box-scrolls-at-the-edge-by-hand-walk (real pointer windowDrag with new holdSeconds: box past the right edge picks recording, song and the title 12 s in; a clip dragged to the edge goes on 7.6 s), zoom-bar-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk. Also green: box-pick-by-hand, box-picks-everything-it-touches, marquee-and-track-range, several-picked-clips-change-track, track-header-lifts(-by-pointer), bar-end-follows-the-pointer, panel-reads-the-marquee, a-zoom-follows-the-cursor.

Tests: the whole suite hung twice in the known HEIF/Vision park (logged on find-out-why-the-whole-test-run-hangs-in-the-mac). Split run all green: --skip Render|Media 11268 pass; Render|Media minus the hang-prone suites 1215 pass; ImageCodec, PackageIO, ReadPageWeightFixture, ReadRunAsTextFixture, ARefusedReadIsToldApart, SoundFile each pass alone.

Frame timing: a 5 s hold deep in runs at 16.7 ms every step (60 fps, none dropped). Full speed across the recording drops about 1 in 20 (p95 33 ms) because each step redraws the whole window; filed scrolling-the-timeline-along-time-keeps-every-fr (p2) with the profile. Left rough, not filed: trims scroll along time only; the layers list drag (LayerRowDragSession) keeps its own quadratic curve since it is not the timeline; walks cannot yet assert the timeline window reading, so it is in the log lines only.

A box, clip, title or zoom bar dragged near any timeline edge now scrolls it (cube curve from a shared tested PhotonzCore helper, EdgeAutoscroll; one 60 Hz display-link driver, TimelineEdgeScroll; track carry moved onto the same curve). Verified at Next defaults by box-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk (right/left/bottom, picks what scrolled in, 5 s hold at 16.7 ms every frame), box-scrolls-at-the-edge-by-hand-walk (real pointer box and clip) and zoom-bar-scrolls-at-the-edge-walk; suite green in the split run. Window no longer snaps back to a still playhead after an edit. Full-speed frame drops filed as scrolling-the-timeline-along-time-keeps-every-fr. Commit ffdf77fc.
